    Week 11 bold predictions: Fernando Mendoza upsets Broncos, Tony Pollard breaks Cowboys

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1492 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Almost anything can happen in the National Football League, and the kickoff to Week 11 of the 2026 season showcased the limits of the league's parity.
    • In the Houston Texans' (4-6) 26-3 road win on the road over the torn-down Indianapolis Colts (3-8), three-time Pro Bowl running back Jonathan Taylor went for just 21 yards rushing on 11 carries.
    • Stroud threw two of his three touchdown passes for 20-plus air yards after having two combined in his first nine games of the 2026 season.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Almost anything can happen in the National Football League, and the kickoff to Week 11 of the 2026 season showcased the limits of the league's parity.

    In the Houston Texans' (4-6) 26-3 road win on the road over the torn-down Indianapolis Colts (3-8), three-time Pro Bowl running back Jonathan Taylor went for just 21 yards rushing on 11 carries. It marked an unfathomable 21 consecutive games without 100 yards rushing in a game, the worst drought of his career. Meanwhile, quarterback Daniel Jones just polished off his sixth straight game with an interception, the longest streak by a Colts player since Curtis Painter was filling in for an injured Peyton Manning in 2011.

    Meanwhile, Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud threw two of his three touchdown passes for 20-plus air yards after having two combined in his first nine games of the 2026 season. Stroud's seven-game streak of multiple total touchdowns is now the longest in Texans history.

    What surprises could occur across the rest of the NFL's Week 11 slate? Let's take a look at five bold predictions.

    It has been revealed that las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza, the first overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, made his debut as an NFL starting quarterback against the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks in Week 10. That made Mendoza the first No. 1 overall pick in NFL history to make his first career start against the defending Super Bowl champion, per CBS Sports Research. He held his own, completing 17 of his 29 throws for 143 yards while also adding 22 yards and a rushing touchdown on six carries. Despite being sacked six times, Mendoza and the Raiders only lost by eight points, 21-13.

    In a recent development, after adjusting to the pace of the NFL game against the Seahawks, Mendoza and the Raiders will head to Empower Field at Mile High Stadium in Denver and emerge victorious against the Broncos. Denver quarterback Bo Nix doesn't scare any defense, ranking last in the league in air yards per pass attempt (5.6). For whatever reason, he can't or won't pull the trigger on throws down the field. Five-time Pro Bowl Raiders edge rusher Maxx Crosby will do enough to spook Nix while Mendoza helps Las Vegas' offense score just enough points for the 10.5-point underdogs, according to DraftKings Sportsbook, to emerge victorious on Sunday.

    According to recent reports, tony Pollard is ascending to new heights at the age of 29 and in the final year of his three-year, $21.75 million contract with the Tennessee Titans. Across his last three games, Pollard has produced 279 yards rushing, 112 yards receiving and six total touchdowns. Even though the Titans had a Week 9 bye, Pollard still ranks in the top 10 in rushing yards, rushing touchdowns, receiving touchdowns and total touchdowns by a running back since Week 7. His five rushing touchdowns are tied for the most in the NFL in this span with Bucky Irving, and his six scrimmage touchdowns in this stretch are tied for the most in the league with Christian McCaffrey.

    It has been revealed that pollard now has his sights set on scoring a touchdown in four consecutive games for the first time in his eight-season NFL career. And just in time for his first matchup with the Dallas Cowboys, the team that drafted him in the fourth round of the 2019 NFL Draft and the team he called home for his first five seasons. His homecoming on Sunday at AT&T Stadium will mark Pollard's first career game against the Cowboys, and he'll have a special day against a Dallas defense that is in total disarray after the half-firing of first-time defensive coordinator Christian Parker on Wednesday. Parker retains his title as defensive coordinator, but head coach Brian Schottenheimer stripped him of defensive play-calling duties and gave them to senior assistant Mike Pettine, a 60-year-old who was retired and vacationing in Italy just a few months ago. Pettine last worked as a defensive play-caller in the NFL in 2020, his final season as the defensive coordinator of the Green Bay Packers.

    Pollard will join Jahmyr Gibbs (twice this season), Bijan Robinson (Week 3 at the Green Bay Packers) and McCaffrey (Week 10 at the Cowboys) as just the fourth player in the entire league this season with 200-plus scrimmage yards and multiple touchdowns in a game on Sunday against his old friends.

    Industry observers note that detroit Lions Pro Bowl running back Jahmyr Gibbs decimated the New England Patriots for 252 yards from scrimmage (153 rushing yards on 22 carries plus 99 yards on seven catches), the most in a game by any player this season. He also added two rushing touchdowns in the Lions' 35-10 stomping of the Patriots in Munich, Germany. What can the league's rushing yards (1,000), scrimmage yards (1,384) and scrimmage touchdowns (13) leader do for Week 11 as an encore against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the NFL's No. 1 run defense?

    The Bucs  are giving up just 79.2 rushing yards per game allowed. But Gibbs will steamroll Buccaneers Pro Bowl defensive tackle Vita Vea and Co. for 120 yards rushing, something that hasn't been done to Tampa Bay since TreVeyon Henderson did so in Week 10 of last season. Do you know who produced the next-most-recent occurrence against the Buccaneers? That's right, it was Gibbs in Week 7 of the 2025 season when he went off for 136 yards rushing and two touchdowns on 17 carries in a 24-9 victory. He'll go over 120 again against the NFL's best run defense on Sunday.

    Sources indicate that the Miami Dolphins head up north to Buffalo to face the 8-1 Bills, the AFC's No. 1 seed, as 16.5-point underdogs per DraftKings Sportsbook. Essentially, the expectation is for the Dolphins to lose by three scores. It's understandable to see why. Bills quarterback Josh Allen has the most total touchdowns in a player's first 10 seasons (325) despite 2026 being just his ninth NFL season. Allen alone has more career playoff touchdowns (39) than Miami's active roster (38) does in the regular season. The Dolphins active roster's 38 combined career touchdowns are the fewest in the NFL by any team's active roster by nearly 50 touchdowns — the Arizona Cardinals are the next-lowest with 85.

    Buffalo is tied for the best record in the NFL along with the San Francisco 49ers at 8-1, while Miami is tied for the worst record at 1-8 with the Titans and the Los Angeles Chargers. However, the Dolphins will lose by only one score on Sunday.

    Recent findings suggest that how is this possible? Well, the Bills have outscored their opponents 90-28 in their last three games while facing five backup quarterbacks: Tyler Huntley, Joe Fagnano, Carson Wentz, Max Brosmer and Cade Klubnik. Yes, the Dolphins are starting one too — 2025 sixth-round pick Kyle McCord — with Malik Willis sidelined, but McCord had a decent debut at theIndianapolis Colts in Week 10. He threw for 209 yards, the second most in an NFL debut in Dolphins history, on 17-of-32 passing with a rushing touchdown and one lost fumble. Rookie third-round wide receiver Caleb Douglas' 367 yards receiving in six games is the most in a player's first six career games in Dolphins history.

    According to recent reports, no team in the last 20 years has seen a higher rate of their snaps (28.8%) go to rookies than the 2026 Dolphins have. They don't know what they don't know. That's why they're going to lose by just one possession against the mighty Bills in Buffalo in Week 11.

    According to recent reports, chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams returns from a Week 10 bye out for blood after throwing four interceptions in Week 9 against the Buccaneers. That snapped his 36-game streak without multiple interceptions, the fourth-longest streak by a starting quarterback since 1950. Williams will be itching to go deep downfield to wide receivers Luther Burden and Rome Odunze to atone for his sloppy play in the last time out.

    According to recent reports, williams' problem is that he is facing one of the best pass-rushing teammate duos in football against the Upcoming Orleans Saints. Saints edge rushers Carl Granderson (8.5 sacks, tied for the second most in the NFL) and Chase Young (8.0 sacks, tied for the fourth-most) have combined for 16.5 sacks, tied for the most of any teammate pass rush duo this season along with the Minnesota Vikings' Andrew Van Ginkel (8.5) and Dallas Turner (8.0).

    Industry observers note that the Saints' defense as a whole hasn't been stellar this season, profiling as the league's No. 25 scoring defense (26.2 points per game allowed), but they'll combine to sack Williams a season-high five times on Sunday. Williams' 3.35-second average time to throw is the longest in the NFL among the league's 31 qualified quarterbacks, which will doom him against Granderson, Young and the New Orleans defense.

    #84824. Youngsters will get their chance, Bruno Fernandes can thrive and touchline energy will be vital: Key lessons for Man United from incoming boss Mauricio Pochettino's 6-0 USA masterclass

    📅 14 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1068 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

    Youngsters will get their chance, Bruno Fernandes can thrive and touchline energy will be vital: Key lessons for Man United from incoming boss Mauricio Pochettino's 6-0 USA masterclass

    📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1068 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Published: 18:47 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 05:54 EST, 16 November 2026.
    • Mauricio Pochettino enjoyed a stellar penultimate game in charge of the United States, thrashing Haiti 6-0.
    • The newly appointed Manchester United manager has just one game left before sinking his teeth into the job at Old Trafford.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Published: 18:47 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 05:54 EST, 16 November 2026.

    Mauricio Pochettino enjoyed a stellar penultimate game in charge of the United States, thrashing Haiti 6-0.

    The newly appointed Manchester United manager has just one game left before sinking his teeth into the job at Old Trafford.

    He will link up with United on Wednesday, but first must navigate the second leg of their Concacaf Nations League quarter-final tie with Haiti on Tuesday.

    Here, Pochettino cut a fairly reserved figure on the touchline as he was rewarded for trusting youth - and even saw his team score from a corner, something United don't do much of these days.

    Without further ado, here are four things Manchester United fans learned from the win.

    Mauricio Pochettino, dressed in a scarf, was fairly reserved as the United States beat Haiti 6-0.

    In a recent development, pochettino’s arrival spells good news for United’s proud tradition of promoting homegrown youth - it is glad tidings for the likes of Shea Lacey and Kobbie Mainoo. You wonder if, for a while, JJ Gabriel will look on forlornly from Real Madrid’s reserves.

    The Argentinian handed out 13 debuts in the September-October international break, including to eight teenagers in one 4-1 victory over Peru.

    His strategy was no different here as he started 18-year-old Julian Hall up front and Diego Kochen, 20, in goal - both players he has given debuts to this year. He was rewarded, with Hall scoring his fourth goal in just five games for the United States, while Kochen kept a clean sheet.

    Sources indicate that despite his affinity for the stars of tomorrow, he is a hard schoolmaster. In a column for The Athletic in 2022, he revealed that he sat a young Harry Kane down for a brutal meeting where he demonstrated him stats and clips to justify why he wasn’t playing him more.

    It has been revealed that pochettino had known Kane’s potential from their first training session but wanted the ‘tough conversation’ to get the best out of him. Kane went on to score 169 goals under him for Tottenham, and now he’s the best player in the world.

    His trust in fresh faces could inject some much-needed enthusiasm around the club, strengthen the squad's connection with the fanbase, and increase the energy levels in one of the Premier League's oldest, most lethargic teams.

    The likes of Shea Lacey will be delighted at how Pochettino puts trust in younger players.

    Julian Hall, 18, struck his fourth goal in five games for the United States under Pochettino.

    Pochettino has a history of getting the most out of attacking midfielders such as Dele Alli, Christian Eriksen, and Adam Lallana. You can add Cole Palmer to that list too, though he was primarily a right winger under him at Chelsea.

    Manchester United desperately need him to get a tune out of Bruno Fernandes, who has cut a frustrated figure this season and whose creative efficiency has declined - though he still has nine goal involvements.

    Industry observers note that if Christian Pulisic’s performance against Haiti is anything to go by, Fernandes will be happy. The attacking midfielder scored twice, playing a free role and being given penalty duty.

    Industry observers note that the 28-year-old was also asked to muck in defensively, and that’s something Fernandes is willing to do. Across the seasons, he has often covered more ground than any of his team-mates.

    According to recent reports, pochettino and Pulisic have seemingly had a distant relationship, despite the latter’s insistence to the contrary. The manager branded it ‘b*******’ when the AC Milan star opted out of the Gold Cup last year, and left him out of his selection a couple of months ago, bringing in 16-year-old Cavan Sullivan.

    Asked about Pochettino's upcoming final game, Pulisic stated at full-time: 'We're treating it like any other game.' No emotion on display.

    Depending on how you interpret Fernandes - either a die-for-the-badge club servant or a primadonna - Pochettino could draw the best or worst out of the Portuguese.

    Pochettino often gets the best out of attacking midfielders - will he work well with Bruno Fernandes?

    He has had a distant relationship with Christian Pulisic, but the AC Milan star scored twice here.

    Pochettino tends to push his defensive lines high up the pitch and his strategy with the United States has been no different.

    They were almost caught out for trying to play the offside trap early on as a simple ball from midfield sent Danley Jean Jacques through one-on-one, forcing Kochen into a good save.

    Meanwhile, full-backs Antonee Robinson and Alex Freeman were constantly pushing high and overlapping in his 4-2-3-1 system - although you’d obviously expect a strong level of intent when they’re favourites against Haiti.

    Given his high-line tradition, Pochettino may well favour more mobile defenders such as Leny Yoro and Patrick Dorgu.

    The battle for Harry Maguire will be to convince his latest boss that his other qualities compensate for his lack of pace.

    Pochettino takes inspiration from the frenetic football of Marcelo Bielsa, who managed him at Newell’s Old Boys in Argentina.

    But he'll have to balance his philosophy with the reality of United's woeful defensive record this campaign. Just the 15 goals conceded in the last five games...

    Pochettino showed an eagerness to intervene early in the game - a possible boost after Michael Carrick suffered from slow starts.

    Pochettino is typically seen as an animated character on the touchline, in contrast to Carrick's statesmanlike behaviour, but he spent lots of time in his seat here.

    He has calmed down somewhat these days - though he did kick a crate of bottles in frustration at the World Cup - and didn’t even react much when his team scored.

    According to recent reports, A major criticism of Carrick is that he takes too long to change things in-game, often going late with substitutions. Pochettino has traditionally leaned that way, too, but he was eager to influence proceedings here.

    Even three minutes in, at a break while Antonee Robinson was being treated, he called Pulisic over for what looked like an intense tactical chat.

    United have been plagued by slow starts this season, so it was encouraging to see Pochettino so alert and full of ideas early into the game. He could have coasted, really, but wanted to eke out every advantage.

    #84823. Breaking: 10 most interesting MLB non-tender decisions, including a Red Sox staple and a former Rookie of the Year

    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: 10 most interesting MLB non-tender decisions, including a Red Sox staple and a former Rookie of the Year

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1649 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, this Friday, Nov.
    • According to recent reports, dozens of players are non-tendered every offseason when teams determine their production no longer warrants the salary.
    • With that in mind, here are the 10 most interesting non-tender decisions ahead of Friday's deadline, using the arbitration salary projections at the indispensable MLB Trade Rumors.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, this Friday, Nov. 20, is an key date on MLB's offseason calendar. It is the deadline for teams to offer 2027 contracts to their arbitration-eligible and pre-arbitration players. The player does not have to sign by Friday's 5 p.m. ET deadline, but he must be offered a contract. If he's not, the player is considered non-tendered and immediately becomes a free agent.

    According to recent reports, dozens of players are non-tendered every offseason when teams determine their production no longer warrants the salary. Adolis García, Nathaniel Lowe, Alek Manoah, and Christopher Morel were among the notable non-tenders last offseason. Go back a few years and big names like Cody Bellinger and Kyle Schwarber were non-tendered.

    With that in mind, here are the 10 most interesting non-tender decisions ahead of Friday's deadline, using the arbitration salary projections at the indispensable MLB Trade Rumors. You can be sure these teams will scour the trade market for these players and try to get something back before making the non-tender official.

    Projected salary: $11.1 million (team control through 2028).

    In a recent development, duran was a non-tender candidate even before the Jake Bauers signing pushed him out of the everyday lineup. There is no such thing as too many good players, but the Red Sox now have two first basemen (Bauers and Willson Contreras) and four outfielders (Duran, Wilyer Abreu, Roman Anthony, Ceddanne Rafaela). Mickey Gasper and Masataka Yoshida are still around too. That's eight players for five lineup spots (first base, DH, three outfield spots). On any given day, three of those guys will be on the bench. Duran, who got MVP votes in 2024, had a 20-20 season in 2026, but it came with a ballooning strikeout rate and a .266 on-base percentage. He has been on the trade block for close to two years now and the writing is on the wall. If the Red Sox are unable to trade Duran this week, there's a real chance he'll get non-tendered Friday given his hefty salary projection.

    Projected salary: $7.7 million (team control through 2028).

    Former No. 1 overall draft picks have been non-tendered in the past (Tim Beckham most recently), just not by the team that drafted them. Non-tendering Torkelson would be a tough look for the Tigers even though he has not developed into the impact hitter he was projected to be coming out of Arizona State. Simply put, the salary is beginning to outweigh the production. Torkelson, 27, is a 25-30 homer bat with one of the league's highest strikeout rates, middling on-base percentages, and no secondary value (defense, baserunning, etc.). That said, the Tigers do not have an obvious replacement first baseman ready to step in (Colt Keith was the backup in 2026). That, plus the fact that Torkelson has No. 1 pick pedigree, could keep him in Detroit another year.

    Projected salary: $2.3 million (team control through 2029).

    The American League Rookie of the Year in 2024, Gil has battled injuries and ineffectiveness in the two seasons since. The swing-and-miss rate on his fastball went from an elite 28.5% in 2024 to a below-average 18.8% in 2025 and 17.4% in 2026. Gil, 28, spent time in Triple-A this past season and the Yankees moved him into the bullpen late in the year, where the results were so-so. The salary projection is a pittance, particularly for a team with Fresh York's payroll, though Gil is now out of minor-league options (he must pass through waivers to go to Triple-A) and doesn't have an obvious role. Because he is a pitcher and breathing, and also has a major award win in the not-too-distant past, the Yankees might be able to find a trade partner this week. If not, Gil is a definite non-tender candidate.

    Projected salary: $7.6 million (team control through 2028).

    It has been revealed that A fan favorite and an All-Star this past season, Clement crashed hard in the second half, and the fact of the matter is he has a .295 on-base percentage in his three full seasons with the Blue Jays. Also, the soon-to-be 31-year-old's defensive numbers tumbled this year. Clement's contact skills are elite and he's a versatile, high-energy player. As a utility guy, he's an ace. As an everyday player, he's stretched. Clement's projected salary is hefty for a utility player, particularly one with limited offensive upside who no longer reliably catches the baseball. My guess is the Blue Jays will keep him and live with the salary, but it's not an obvious decision.

    Projected salary: $5.1 million (team control through 2028).

    According to recent reports, similar to Torkelson, non-tendering a former No. 1 overall pick would be a tough look for the Twins, but a clean break might be best for all involved at this point. Lewis, 27, has trended down since his boffo second half in 2023, enough that he was sent to Triple-A for a spell this summer. He's also moved down the defensive spectrum from third base to first base. It's not due to a lack of effort; Lewis is a major tinkerer who has tried all sorts of swing adjustments. It just hasn't come together. A fresh start elsewhere, away from the spotlight of former No. 1 pick and face of the franchise, might be best for him. The budget-conscious Twins could then reallocate the projected $5.1 million elsewhere on the roster. Right now, they can't count on Lewis to hit or have a meaningful impact defensively.

    Projected salary: $3.4 million (team control through 2028).

    Recent findings suggest that in 2023, Gorman slugged 27 home runs and looked like one of baseball's top young power hitters. In the three seasons since, he has not come close to repeating that success. The hope was that moving him to third base, his natural position, would unlock Gorman's offense following the Nolan Arenado trade. That didn't happen, and Gorman spent a massive chunk of the summer in Triple-A, where he continued to have a hard time making contact. Now 26, Gorman has a minor-league option remaining and can go to Triple-A again in 2027, but the signs are not subtle. The Cardinals are reportedly seeking a stopgap third baseman until top prospect Jesús Báez is ready, which would likely not be the case if they had any belief in Gorman. That projected $3.4 million salary is a high price for a reclamation project ticketed for the minors.

    Projected salary: $6.9 million (team control through 2028).

    Right-handed power is in short supply throughout baseball and Burger, 31 in April, has hit at least 28 home runs in three of the last four years. He is a one-tool player, though. The home runs come with low batting averages, low on-base percentages, higher-than-average strikeout rates, and little to no defensive or baserunning value. Rangers president of baseball operations Chris Young said his team lacked "grit and toughness," whatever that means, and indicated he wants more hitters who grind out at-bats. That's not Burger, who can hit the ball a mile but is not known for making life tough on pitchers. The $6.9 million projection could be deemed too pricey for a player with such a limited skill set.

    Projected salary: $6.6 million (team control through 2027).

    In a recent development, doval went from the Yankees to the Pirates at the trade deadline, then from the Pirates to the Giants on waivers in September. He's a former All-Star who led the National League in saves in 2023, two things that have boosted his arbitration salaries. Since 2023, Doval has been a middle reliever who was on the outside of the Circle of Trust™ more often than not. The 29-year-old righty still throws very hard. There's nothing wrong with his arm. It's hard to believe he gets hit as hard as he does sometimes. Doval earned $6.1 million in 2026 and a player cannot have a salary cut by more than 20% during his team control years. That would set Doval's minimum 2027 salary at $4.88 million. I wonder if the Giants would offer him a pay cut, say $5.5M or so, and tell him it's either that or a non-tender. That happens a few times a year around the league.

    Projected salary: $6.5 million (team control through 2027).

    Sources indicate that A fan favorite in San Diego -- "Ho-ly Sheets!" chants are commonplace during his at-bats at Petco Park -- Sheets has fallen by the wayside a bit with the Padres, so much so that he started just one of their six postseason games this year. The 30-year-old is a platoon player who is good against righties more than great and is a defensive liability at both first base and left field. Realistically, Sheets is a platoon DH, and teams rarely pay well for that role unless they're confident they will get significant offensive numbers. In the grand scheme of things, the projected $6.5 million isn't much. It is top-of-the-market dollars for this skill set, however.

    Projected salary: $1.4 million (team control through 2029).

    Two years ago, Blanco threw a no-hitter in his eighth career start. This year, he was so far out of the picture that he pitched once in Houston's last 12 games (two innings at the end of a 13-2 blowout), and the Astros opted to start Peter Lambert on two days' rest with a postseason spot on the line in Game 162. Blanco, who is older than you may realize (he turned 33 in August), returned from Tommy John surgery this summer and had a rough go of it. The pitching-needy Astros could send him to Triple-A next season, as he has a minor-league option remaining, but his stuff was diminished after surgery, and again, they didn't trust him late in the year. You would be surprised at how many cheap pitchers get non-tendered every year. Blanco could join them this week.

    The Philadelphia 76ers are off to a fantastic start to the 2026-27 season at 12-3, good for first in the Eastern Conference, and perhaps most encouraging for the Sixers is that they're winning without looking like a team playing at its absolute peak.

    Sources indicate that after a huge offseason adding LeBron James and Jaylen Brown, the Sixers still look like a team figuring out how best to work together, but when it comes time in the fourth quarter to find a way to win, they manage to get the job done. Tyrese Maxey is leading the way with Brown swiftly finding his rhythm, but James and Joel Embiid in particular still seem to be feeling it out early in the season.

    James, who has never averaged less than 20.9 points per game in his previous 23 seasons, is averaging just 15.1 points per game and his 44.3/22.5/71.7 shooting splits are all career lows or close to it. As James figures things out, ESPN reported that a Sixers source claimed James "asked coaches to be patient with him as he expects to find his rhythm and get his conditioning in line by December as he ramps up.".

    That report hit social media and caught James' attention, with the 41-year-old star denying ever saying that.

    ESPN didn't report a direct quote from James, and it's very possible the Sixers source offered an anecdote that paraphrased James and used the word patience when James never did. That then ended up on a social media graphic and prompted James to shoot it down.

    Recent findings suggest that what's fascinating here is it's not a scathing report or even anything particularly juicy. James is struggling with his shot early in the year and seems to be figuring out exactly where he fits in the offense alongside Maxey, Brown and Embiid as a scorer. He's still doing plenty of things well -- including leading the team with 6.9 assists per game and just took over third all-time in assists in NBA history -- and the Sixers are still winning even with James ice cold with his jumper, which history suggests will turn around at some point.

    Patience would be prudent from the Sixers with James, whether he wants to use that word or not, and it seems like a matter of when, not if, he gets shots to start falling and the Philly offense becomes even more dynamic.

    Latest Update: NFL exploring possibility of implementing new travel rules for international games

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (702 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • With the NFL's uptick in international games over the last few years, there's no rule requiring a team to arrive in a foreign city by a certain date before a game, but that could change.
    • The NFL is currently exploring a latest travel policy that would require each team to spend a minimum number of nights in an international city.
    • "Currently, we leave those football decisions on when the team arrives in the market to the club," O'Reilly said.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    With the NFL's uptick in international games over the last few years, there's no rule requiring a team to arrive in a foreign city by a certain date before a game, but that could change. That could change soon.

    The NFL is currently exploring a latest travel policy that would require each team to spend a minimum number of nights in an international city. In an interview this week with The Athletic, NFL executive VP of club business Peter O'Reilly confirmed that a change could be coming.

    "Currently, we leave those football decisions on when the team arrives in the market to the club," O'Reilly said. "It is something that we'll consider moving forward on: Do we put some minimum nights in a market in there? It's something we'll look at.".

    Recent findings suggest that it's no surprise the NFL is thinking hard about this topic, especially after what happened in Week 1 during the league's first regular-season game in Australia between the 49ers and the Rams. The 49ers decided to fly out a full week before the game so they could acclimate to the 17-hour time difference. Leaving early also allowed the team to fully immerse themselves in Australian culture.

    On the other hand, the Rams infamously didn't arrive until the last minute: They landed in Melbourne at about 7 a.m. ET on Thursday morning, leaving them less than 30 hours until their game with the 49ers kicked off.

    The Rams traveled late so that their players wouldn't have to adjust to Australian time, but the plan backfired. The Rams looked slow and tired during a 27-7 loss.

    Industry observers note that if the NFL does implement a minimum-night rule, it likely won't be anything dramatic. The rule that would make the most sense is having teams arrive at least two nights in advance. For a game in Europe, that would mean a team would have to leave Thursday night to arrive Friday.

    Industry observers note that that exact travel plan was not only popular this year, but also successful. In fact, teams traveling to Europe went 4-0 this year when arriving on Friday. The Steelers, Texans, Colts, and Jaguars (for their first London game) all arrived Friday morning for their international game, and all four teams won. It's hard to imagine the NFL creating a rule to eliminate something that's working well for teams, so if the league implements a upcoming travel policy, it likely won't be a massive change.

    In a recent development, since international play started in 2007, there are only three instances of a team showing up the day before a game in a city at least five time zones away, and the Rams were involved in two of them. The Rams arrived on Saturday in London for a 35-7 blowout win over the Jaguars in 2025, which is why they likely felt good about arriving the day before the game in Australia this year. The Eagles ended up copying the Rams' strategy for their game in London this year, arriving on Saturday for their matchup against the Jags, which ended up being a dramatic 19-17 loss.

    Industry observers note that there were a total of nine international games this year, and the final one will be played in Mexico City on Sunday night between the Vikings and the 49ers. If the NFL does implement a fresh travel policy, it will be interesting to see whether it includes games like this that are geographically closer to the United States. The Vikings are flying down to the game on Saturday because the flight from Minnesota to Mexico City is only about 4.5 hours and there's no time zone change, so it's not necessarily a reason to travel early (The stadium in Mexico City does have an altitude of 7,350 feet, so it could make sense to travel early to get acclimated to that, but the Vikings decided not to go that route).

    Under the current CBA, the NFL is allowed to schedule up to 10 international games for 2027, and if the league hits that number, it will certainly be interesting to see if a fresh travel policy is in place for next season.

    Liverpool have been handed a significant double injury boost in the days leading up to their Premier League clash against Manchester United.

    Andoni Iraola will be pleased that his players who were on international duty all seem set to return to Merseyside unscathed, even though Dominik Szoboszlai controversially played through the pain barrier for Hungary.

    The Reds’ head coach is still waiting for a handful of long-term injury absentees to become available once more, but two of those have now taken a major step in their respective recoveries.

    As reported by Paul Joyce for The Times, Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni have returned to Liverpool first-team training, with both defenders having been sidelined for a number of months with serious knee injuries.

    The Northern Ireland right-back has been out of action since January after he was struck down towards the end of the 0-0 draw at Arsenal; while the Italian teenager has been absent for even longer, not playing since rupturing his ACL on his Reds debut in September 2025.

    The latter had been due to resume full training in early October before that staging post was delayed as medical staff took a cautious approach, but he’s now in the final stages of his recovery to full fitness and could resume playing in the coming weeks.

    In a recent development, want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

    While we wouldn’t bank on either of the Liverpool duo returning to matchday action in the concluding weeks of 2026, their resumption of first-team training comes as a huge step towards their long-awaited comebacks.

    Bradley would very likely have made the right-back position his own this season had he not been sidelined, but thankfully Ronald Araujo has excelled in that role since joining on loan from Barcelona in August.

    As for Leoni, it was beyond cruel that he tore his ACL towards the end of what had been a terrific Reds debut against Southampton 14 months ago, but he’s still only 19 and should hopefully have a hugely successful career still ahead of him.

    Even when both players are cleared for a return to action, it’ll take time for them to properly get back into a matchday rhythm, and Iraola will surely bed them in gently after missing so much football over the past few months.

    However, having them back in a full training feels like a significant step forward, and when the time comes for them to resume playing, it’ll be a wonderful sight for everyone associated with Liverpool.

    2027 Baseball Hall of Fame ballot released: 8 things to know, including newcomers, trends and a prediction

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1174 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The ballot for the BBWAA portion of the 2027 Baseball Hall of Fame vote was revealed on Monday, featuring 13 holdovers and 14 newcomers.
    • The full ballot, in alphabetical order, is Bobby Abreu, Jake Arrieta, Jay Bruce, Mark Buehrle, Asdrúbal Cabrera, Starlin Castro, Wade Davis, Brett Gardner, Cole Hamels, Félix Hernández, Torii Hunter, Jon Lester, Andrew Miller, Dustin Pedroia, Andy Pettitte, Buster Posey, Alex Rodriguez, Francisco Rodríguez, Jimmy Rollins, Pablo Sandoval, Ervin Santana, Kyle Seager, Joakim Soria, Chase Utley, Omar Vizquel, David Wright and Ryan Zimmerman.
    • Industry observers note that as a reminder, players must receive votes on at least 75% of the ballots cast to be inducted into the Hall of Fame with the 2027 class.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The ballot for the BBWAA portion of the 2027 Baseball Hall of Fame vote was revealed on Monday, featuring 13 holdovers and 14 newcomers.

    The full ballot, in alphabetical order, is Bobby Abreu, Jake Arrieta, Jay Bruce, Mark Buehrle, Asdrúbal Cabrera, Starlin Castro, Wade Davis, Brett Gardner, Cole Hamels, Félix Hernández, Torii Hunter, Jon Lester, Andrew Miller, Dustin Pedroia, Andy Pettitte, Buster Posey, Alex Rodriguez, Francisco Rodríguez, Jimmy Rollins, Pablo Sandoval, Ervin Santana, Kyle Seager, Joakim Soria, Chase Utley, Omar Vizquel, David Wright and Ryan Zimmerman. Newcomers to the ballot are in bold.

    Industry observers note that as a reminder, players must receive votes on at least 75% of the ballots cast to be inducted into the Hall of Fame with the 2027 class. Those who get at least 5% of the vote can remain on the ballot the following year, and so on, for a maximum of 10 voting cycles. Players who are on the ballot for 10 years without getting 75% of the vote, in addition to players not getting 5% of the vote, fall off the ballot in ensuing years, though that doesn't mean the doors to the Hall are permanently shut.

    The results will be confirmed on Jan. 19, with the induction set for Cooperstown over the summer.

    Here's everything else you need to know about the Baseball Hall of Fame this offseason.

    Recent findings suggest that as alluded to earlier, there are two different votes each offseason. The BBWAA vote is for former players who have been retired from Major League Baseball for at least five years. It's the most common method in mainstream Hall of Fame ballot discussions. When you hear stuff like "first-ballot Hall of Famer," it means via the BBWAA vote.

    Players who don't make it via the BBWAA vote can get extra chances via committees. That's how, for example, Jeff Kent made it last year. Formerly called the Veterans Committee, the Hall of Fame now uses Era Committees, which are divided into two categories: contemporary baseball (1980 to present) and classic (prior to 1980). The contemporary ballot is then split into two, one for players and one for non-players like umpires, executives, pioneers and managers.

    Sure enough, this time around, it is a non-player Contemporary Baseball Committee, which looks at "managers, umpires and executives whose most significant career impact was realized since 1980.".

    According to recent reports, we'll dive further into this group as we get closer to the Dec. 6 vote.

    Giants legend Buster Posey joins the ballot, and he's one of those cases where I don't think a bunch of people need to delve deeply into his numbers. More than statistics, sometimes we get "feel" guys, as in, you just know he's a Hall of Famer. Posey qualifies there, I would think, for 75% of the electorate. We'll obviously do a deeper dive in the coming weeks, but even without the longevity component (Posey only played in parts of 12 MLB seasons), I think he's in.

    As for the rest of the first-timers, the best case would be Jon Lester. Given the way a lot of similar starting pitchers have been treated in voting in recent years, my hunch is he'll be able to hang around on the ballot, but he has a major uphill battle in order to get in.

    Recent findings suggest that then you're looking at Brett Gardner, Ryan Zimmerman, Kyle Seager, the short peak of Jake Arrieta and relief work of Andrew Miller. Good players worth mentioning, of course, but they won't sniff the Hall and it seems likely all behind Posey and Lester are one-and-dones on this ballot, as they'll fall short of 5% of the vote.

    This is the sixth year for Alex Rodriguez on the ballot, which means it's the sixth time that I point out that we don't really need much time to go over his case. His numbers say he's one of the 10 best position players of all time, but his ties to PEDs are keeping him out to this point.

    He did rise from 37.1% of the vote in 2025 to 40% last time, a new high-water mark. The progress is too modest to believe it's trending toward him getting in, but the number this year is certainly worth watching. If he somehow makes a leap to the 50% range, a deeper conversation might be in order.

    It has been revealed that while some voters don't mind sending in blank ballots to prove some sort of nebulous point, most impose limits on themselves. Whether it's the actual rule of 10 or some voters saying they'll only vote, for example, for a maximum of three players on any given ballot, relatively weak ballots can leave openings for the best players to show huge gains. With Carlos Beltràn and Andruw Jones getting in last year and only one strong first-year candidate, perhaps Chase Utley can benefit.

    Utley is only in his fourth year on the ballot, but he's already made significant gains:.

    It has been revealed that he only needs to add 15.9 points after jumping nearly 20 last voting cycle. The situation is ripe for Utley to either get all the way in or get close enough to where he probably makes the Hall of Fame in 2028.

    Some of us are pushing to lower the Hall of Fame standard on modern starting pitchers, given the decreases in workload and how it affects their career numbers. We might be making some headway, but it's still tough sledding. Here are the holdover starting pitchers and their standing:.

    The bar for relievers to make the Hall of Fame is justly pretty high. We recently saw Billy Wagner make a late move and make it in his last try on the BBWAA ballot. Francisco Rodríguez has had four chances on the ballot and gotten between 7.8% and 11.8% of the vote thus far.

    K-Rod ranks sixth all time in saves and has good rate stats. He's worth tracking as it relates to three active relievers. Kenley Jansen is third in saves with a similar number of innings pitched to K-Rod. Craig Kimbrel is fifth and has more than 100 fewer innings pitched. Aroldis Chapman is ninth and in the ballpark of Kimbrel in workload to this point.

    It has been revealed that if K-Rod continues to have trouble making headway toward induction, does that mean Kimbrel and Chapman will have trouble as well? What about Jansen?

    Industry observers note that who else is back on the ballot? A quick look:.

    According to recent reports, posey is a lock. If the committee era chooses Bochy, Baker and/or Sabean, that would be some nice San Francisco flavor, too, right? I'll predict that committee ballot at a later date, though.

    I'll also say Utley's good roll here continues with a relatively weak ballot (at least when you factor in what the PED stain has done to some guys).

    On the player side, my 2027 Hall of Fame class prediction is Buster Posey and Chase Utley.

    Breaking: NBA MVP Rankings: Luka Dončić, Victor Wembanyama in a two-horse race; Stephen Curry's absence speaks volumes

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1535 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • We're nearly a month into the 2026-27 NBA season, and while some people say it's too early to start talking about MVP, we are not among those people.
    • Right now, it's a clear two-horse race: Luka Doncic or Victor Wembanyama?
    • The Luka Dončić we're watching right now isn't just the best offensive player in the world.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    We're nearly a month into the 2026-27 NBA season, and while some people say it's too early to start talking about MVP, we are not among those people.

    Right now, it's a clear two-horse race: Luka Doncic or Victor Wembanyama? There is a real split on this. Here's where I stand as of Tuesday, Nov. 17.

    The Luka Dončić we're watching right now isn't just the best offensive player in the world. He might be the best in history. Nobody has ever put up anything close to the numbers he is charting at the moment: 39 points per game with seven assists, seven boards, nearly two steals and a positively scorching 66.0 TS%, the latter being a number even the great Stephen Curry has only bested twice in his career.

    It's early, sure. Dončić isn't likely to keep making 3s at this rate for an entire season, and indeed we've seen some slippage of late (35% over his last four, if you really want to split hairs), but his volume remains, with 4.5 makes a night over that stretch. Dončić remains on track to break Curry's single-season record of 402 3-pointers, and he's done more off-ball shooting than in the past.

    In a recent development, throw in more transition production and a 53% midrange conversion rate, per Cleaning The Glass, and you're seeing a more diverse scorer, which is to say this isn't just a guy who has started off hot on his step-back 3s (though this is a major factor, too, of course), but a guy piercing defenses from more spots with different shots. If Dončić could actually be any harder to guard than he has been in the past, we're seeing it this season.

    Recent findings suggest that he's also defending. His 23 steals rank sixth league-wide. Only two players have recovered more defensive loose balls than his eight. Only one has taken more charges than his four. With Dončić as the primary defender, shooters are converting just 36.7% of their shots against a 45.1 expected FG%; that minus-8.6 is the fourth-largest discrepancy among all players who've contested at least 150 shots.

    Most importantly, the Lakers are 12-2 and tied with the Spurs atop the Western Conference. The Lakers rank as the league's top offense with a rating that balloons to 129.2 points per 100 possessions (which would be an NBA record by a long shot) with Dončić on, and a net rating, as illustrated below, that falls off a cliff when he sits.

    It has been revealed that look, if you have Wembanyama ahead of Dončić in the MVP race a month into the season, nobody is going to argue much with you. The oddsmakers slightly favor Wembanyama (+110 at FanDuel; Dončić is +140), who, as you'll see below, has what would qualify as a potentially unanimous case in most years. But this isn't most years. We got a dude averaging nearly 40 points for a No. 1 seed that nobody expected to be a No. 1 seed. Until one of those things changes, it's hard for me to go against Dončić.

    If you think Dončić's plus-35.5 on/off split (it's actually plus-32.2 without filtering for garbage time) is crazy, have a look at Wembanyama's number.

    Sources indicate that victor Wembanyama's impact this season has been another level. Spurs are +42.6 points per 100 possessions with Wemby on the court than off it, according to @cleantheglass. Small sample but other-worldly. Lakers star Luka Dončić is at +35.5 pts/100 poss.Both numbers are better… pic.twitter.com/0GJCFFmZ5K.

    In a recent development, yes, you're reading that right. The Spurs, for all their supportive talent, fall by 42.6 points per 100 possessions when Wembanyama leaves the court (plus-29.2 on vs. minus-13.3 off), per Cleaning the Glass. By comparison, the best on/off split that Nikola Jokić has ever recorded is plus-24.8. Curry's best is plus-21.3. LeBron James' is plus-17.8. Go down that list and look at the most impactful on-off splits those guys have ever posted. Wembanyama is in another galaxy.

    And it's important to note that Wembanyama plays on a great team, as all these guys in the graphic have. The fact that there is still so much difference between when Wembanyama is on the court and when he isn't, even in a small sample, is honestly difficult to comprehend. San Antonio's three-guard lineup was supposed to be an experiment, but it's hard to know if Dylan Harper, De'Aaron Fox and Stephon Castle truly optimize one another or if Wembanyama is enough to make any lineup dominant in spite of traditional problems (like none of those three being a true shooter).

    Sources indicate that wembanyama is the best defensive player on the planet by an immeasurable amount. Even the stats don't do it justice. He's on pace for north of 350 blocks, a number only four players (Elmore Smith, Mark Eaton, Manute Bol and Hakeem Olajuwon) have eclipsed since blocks became an official stat in 1973, and still it's just as much, if not more, about the shots he deters scorers from even attempting.

    It has been revealed that and why would they? Scorers are making just 33.6% of their shots when Wembanyama is the nearest defender, a 17% drop from their expected 50.4%. That also leads the league among all players who've defended at least 120 shots, and again, it fails to fully capture his defensive dominance.

    The fact that we've gotten this far without talking about Wembanyama's offense, as if it's a mere afterthought for a guy to be averaging 28.6 points and 11.6 rebounds in under 30 minutes a night. Wembanyama is figuring out his hot spots, prioritizing closer-to-the-basket positioning where he is a skyscraper among regular NBA buildings. He's taking two more paint shots per game than he did last season; 43% of his shots are coming from inside four feet, per Cleaning the Glass, up from 38% last season, and his 4.6 dunks per game (up from 2.7 last year) have him on pace to shatter Rudy Gobert's single-season record of 306.

    Industry observers note that if I had to guess, Wembanyama's production is more sustainable than Dončić's. It's hard to imagine Dončić not hitting a rough patch from 3, and he's almost certainly not going to keep scoring 39 points per game. He'll be over 35 points per game when everything is said and done because that's what the Lakers need from him, but there's a burnout factor while Wembanyama is kind of cruising to these numbers, and the defensive impact is as natural as breathing. My gut indicates Wembanyama will be a clearer MVP favorite by Christmas.

    Assuming Dončić and Wembanyama each get to the mandated 65 games, everyone else is playing for third place at the moment. Which is crazy given the seasons some of the following names are having.

    Recent findings suggest that one of two players averaging at least 22 points, nine rebounds and seven assists, and the only player to be leading his team in all three categories. The Rockets are 11-4 with the No. 2 offense and Sengun is the center of it all.

    Tatum is averaging his normal 26.5 points per game. The shooting efficiency still hasn't come around, but he is an absolute quarterback on this Celtics team. He draws the doubles, and his 35.1% assist rate, per CTG, is a career high by a mile. The Celtics, for my money, are the best team in the East.

    It has been revealed that cunningham is, once again, doing everything for the Pistons, who have been without Jalen Duren for all but the first four games and are still a top-three East seed. The 3-point shooting is down, but that's splitting hairs. This guy is shot-creating machine and, as forceful as he plays, he makes it look as smooth as anyone in the league.

    Recent findings suggest that here come the Heat, who have won five straight games, with the last three wins coming over the Cavaliers, Pistons and Rockets. Antetokounmpo is averaging 28.3/12.5/5.2 with 1.3 blocks per game on 60% shooting. He's on fire from the midrange as the Heat are exploiting the soft spots in all the drop coverage they're facing.

    According to recent reports, gilgeous-Alexander has so much on his plate that it actually creates a clearer path to a third straight MVP if he can somehow lift Oklahoma City above all these injuries. He's trying. The Thunder are 9-5 and he's getting his 30.9 points per game, but his 58.7 true-shooting is down considerably, which makes sense as he has to force tougher shots now with fewer weapons around him.

    According to recent reports, curry's value can perhaps be felt most in his absence. The Warriors have lost three straight since he went out with a torn oblique, the last two by 59 points. The Warriors have outscored opponents by 13.5 points per 100 possessions with Curry on the floor this season and have been outscored by 8.3 points per 100 possessions without him. Along with Yaxel Lendeborg, who's being asked as a rookie to carry an impossibly heavy weight without Curry, Curry remains the only real lifeblood of a team that is still shockingly lifeless without him.

    • The Premier League’s Key Match Incidents (KMI) Panel has adjudged that Liverpool had a penalty wrongly given against them in a recent fixture.
    • The Reds won their last game before the international break, beating Crystal Palace 3-1 at Selhurst Park, although Alisson Becker was denied a clean sheet by a stoppage-time spot kick awarded to the home side and converted by Eddie Nketiah.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Premier League’s Key Match Incidents (KMI) Panel has adjudged that Liverpool had a penalty wrongly given against them in a recent fixture.

    The Reds won their last game before the international break, beating Crystal Palace 3-1 at Selhurst Park, although Alisson Becker was denied a clean sheet by a stoppage-time spot kick awarded to the home side and converted by Eddie Nketiah.

    The penalty was awarded for what referee Tony Harrington deemed to be a foul by Milos Kerkez on Dario Osorio when the two players unfortunately clashed heads, and Andoni Iraola said afterwards that he was ‘very upset‘ over that decision.

    The Premier League’s KMI Panel has now published its findings from the most recent top-flight matchday (via premierleague.com), and all five independent assessors adjudged that the penalty award against Liverpool was incorrect.

    However, there was also unanimous agreement that VAR was right not to intervene, as it was decreed that no ‘clear and obvious’ error had taken place.

    The panel concluded: ‘The panel unanimously felt that the referee’s call of a penalty for a challenge by Kerkez on Osorio was incorrect, with the contact being inevitable given the jumping actions of both players.

    ‘However, the non-intervention of VAR was supported on the basis it was not a clear and obvious error.’.

    Recent findings suggest that want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

    Liverpool fans must be getting sick of hearing from the Premier League’s KMI Panel at this stage, with this incident coming fresh off the back of the panel ruling that we should’ve had a penalty for Jurrien Timber’s blatant shirt pull on Alexander Isak in the 0-1 defeat to Arsenal.

    The incident with Kerkez and Osorio wasn’t as black-and-white, but the decision to award a spot kick still felt rather curious at the time. Luckily for Harrington, it came too late to have any major bearing on the overall result at Selhurst Park.

    Still, to hear that an independent panel unanimously acknowledged that the Reds were wronged by another refereeing error is galling for everyone associated with LFC, and yet again it calls into question the standads of officiating in the Premier League.

    It’s the kind of inconsistency between Kerkez having a spot kick given against him for a 50/50 duel, and Timber getting away with a blatant infringement, which drives players, coaches, fans and pundits absolutely berserk.

    Thankfully the decision in the Palace game didn’t do any lasting harm for Liverpool, but you get the sense that it won’t be long before another contentious decision goes against us and the KPI Panel is wheeled out to tell us what we can already deduce for ourselves.

    Welcome to our Live Comments section, where new comments will appear automatically.

    It was a clear and obvious mistake by the ref. I doubt anyone has seen a penalty awarded for an innocent clash of heads, so why was it that VAR ignored it? Incompetence by the referee and VAR or something else? Fed up with seeing such terrible officiating.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • For the first three years of his NFL career, Detroit Lions three-time Pro Bowl running back Jahmyr Gibbs was known as part of one of the NFL's best running back tandems, the "Sonic" in the Lions' "Sonic and Knuckles" duo with David Montgomery.
    • Yes, that sounds hyperbolic, but Gibbs' production is at all-time levels through three-and-a-half seasons.
    • Sources indicate that just halfway through his fourth season, Gibbs passed Pro Football Hall of Famer Terrell Davis (61 touchdowns in his first four seasons) for the most touchdowns in a player's first four seasons in NFL history (62 and counting).
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    For the first three years of his NFL career, Detroit Lions three-time Pro Bowl running back Jahmyr Gibbs was known as part of one of the NFL's best running back tandems, the "Sonic" in the Lions' "Sonic and Knuckles" duo with David Montgomery. Today, Gibbs is showing that, as a solo act, not only can he can be the NFL's No. 1 back, but he's also laying the early groundwork to become one of the greatest running backs of all time.

    Yes, that sounds hyperbolic, but Gibbs' production is at all-time levels through three-and-a-half seasons. On an international stage in Week 10, he erupted for 252 yards from scrimmage (153 rushing yards on 22 carries plus 99 yards on 7 catches), the most in a game by any player this season, and 2 rushing touchdowns in the Lions' 35-10 stomping of the Fresh England Patriots in Munich, Germany. An outing like that reshuffles some NFL record boards.

    Sources indicate that just halfway through his fourth season, Gibbs passed Pro Football Hall of Famer Terrell Davis (61 touchdowns in his first four seasons) for the most touchdowns in a player's first four seasons in NFL history (62 and counting). Gibbs is also now the first player in NFL history with 1,000 rushing yards (exactly 1,000) and 350 receiving yards (384) in a player's first nine games of a season. With an NFL-best 1,384 yards from scrimmage and a league-high13 scrimmage touchdowns in nine games, Gibbs is on pace for an NFL single-season record: 2,614 yards from scrimmage, which would smash current record holder Chris Johnson's 2,509 from the 2009 season.

    Industry observers note that all of those feats are jaw-dropping on their own, but together they paint an all-time picture. What is perhaps most amazing about Gibbs is how consistently excellent he is, to the point that the football world is somewhat numb to his greatness. Producing 150-plus rushing yards and a rushing touchdown in a game is outstanding. Six players have produced such a game this season, but five of the six have done so no more than twice. Then there is Gibbs, who has done so four times in Detroit's first nine games, making him just the fourth player in NFL history to do so. The other three are a who's who of Hall of Fame running backs: Jim Brown (1958, 1963), O.J. Simpson (1974, 1975) and Emmitt Smith (1995).

    Now, some people might feel Gibbs' historic start to his NFL career is amplified by a talent offensive ecosystem that has a five-time Pro Bowler at quarterback, Jared Goff, a four-time Pro Bowler at wide receiver (Amon-Ra St. Brown), a Pro Bowl tight end (Sam LaPorta), a four-time Pro Bowl offensive tackle (Penei Sewell), and a speedster No. 2 wide receiver (Jameson Williams). However, Gibbs and his consistent excellence power everything else in the Motor City team's offense. He ranks seventh in the league in yards before contact per rush (1.57) and eighth in yards after contact per rush (3.5) this season.

    Among the 27 players with at least 100 carries in 2026, Gibbs' 29.1% tackles-avoided rate is the second-best in the league, behind only Kenneth Walker III's 32.1% rate. Since Next Gen Stats began tracking explosive runs (runs of 10 or more yards) in 2016, no running back has produced more through the first 10 weeks of a season than Gibbs' 34. Prime Ezekiel Elliott in his rookie year with the Dallas Cowboys in 2016 is the closest player in this span with 29. Gibbs isn't just a cog in the Lions' machine: his juice powers the rest of the machine.

    In a recent development, here's the cherry on top. Not even through his fourth NFL season, Gibbs has more games (two) with 250-plus scrimmage yards and multiple touchdowns in his 58-game career than Barry Sanders, the running back many believe is the best pure runner ever, did in his 10-season, 153-game career.

    Week 11 gives Gibbs a chance to deliver an all-time encore performance in a matchup against Pro Bowl defensive tackle Vita Vea and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the No. 1 run defense in the NFL (79.2 rushing yards per game allowed) this season. Get your popcorn ready as Gibbs continues to build a strong case for being the league's most productive running back ever.

Those of us wanting a flurry of moves before the CBA expires on Dec. 1 are starting to lose a little hope, but hey, it's still possible. We can start with a fresh batch of rumors and wait for something to come to fruition.

    Recent findings suggest that as for the news and rumors for Monday, Nov. 16, let's go.

    The Orioles are "operating with the intent of adding" a left-handed starting pitcher, according to the Baltimore Banner. They have extended a qualifying offer to Trevor Rogers and though he's expected to decline it, a reunion remains possible. If not, the Orioles are also reportedly interested in lefty free agents Kris Bubic, Matthew Boyd and David Peterson.

    Rogers is the best option here. He finished last season with a 2.90 ERA in his last 20 starts. CBS Sports ranked him as the No. 3 free agent this offseason and the best non-Tarik Skubal pitcher on the market. Here's part of the write-up:.

    Rogers was never able to fully work off the early season stinkers that inflated his ERA, though this is free agency, and ERA is close to the last thing on the minds of interested teams. You're looking forward in free agency, not backward. The underlying performance indicators are very strong, specifically the ability to get chase and avoid the barrel with four pitches (four-seamer, sinker, changeup, sweeper) that light up analytical models. Rogers also has a fifth-pitch cutter and has shown the ability to hammer the strike zone the last two years.

    As things stand, the Orioles' rotation starts with right-handers Kyle Bradish and Shane Baz. Cade Povich is a left-handed option, but they'd clearly like someone else who could qualify as a frontline starter from the left-handed side.

    In a recent development, former Cy Young winner Sandy Alcantara has been involved in trade rumors for years and the Marlins never end up moving him. More of the same this offseason? Probably.

    "I expect Sandy to be on the Marlins next year," general manager Peter Bendix told MLB Network.

    Alcantara, 31, was 13-11 with a 3.87 ERA, 1.23 WHIP and 153 strikeouts in an MLB-best 214 innings last season. He also grabbed three saves down the stretch as the Marlins started experimenting with using starters in relief on their bullpen day between starts. The 2022 Cy Young winner missed all of 2024 after having Tommy John surgery and started to show flashes of his old self last season. He's now making $21 million in 2027 before hitting free agency.

    If the Marlins contend, he'll surely stay put, but if they fall out of contention, it'll be another round of trade rumors.

    Free agent left-hander A.J. Minter is getting a lot of interest, per MLB Network. Coming off a season in which he was productive for both the Mets and Twins (in all, a 2.56 ERA, 1.05 WHIP and 41 strikeouts in 45 ⅔ innings), he's being chased by at least the Blue Jays, Nationals, Phillies, Rangers and Royals.

    In a recent development, though he's closed on occasion, Minter has been a quality setup man for most of his 10 MLB years, especially with the Braves in the 2020-24 range. He has good playoff numbers, too, with a 2.88 ERA in 20 career postseason appearances.

    The Brewers have acquired right-handed reliever Ryan Walker from the Giants for two minor-league pitchers, the team revealed late Sunday. Walker, 30, was up and down in his four years with the Giants, which included time as a closer. He had a 1.91 ERA, 10 saves and 2.8 WAR in 2024, but lost the job of closer during a sub-par 2025 season. Last year, he pitched to a 7.16 ERA and 1.81 WHIP in 32 ⅔ innings.

    We have plenty of examples of the Brewers buying low on a player and ending up getting the best version of him, so Walker is the latest to keep an eye on here.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Published: 09:50 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 06:26 EST, 16 November 2026.
    • Erling Haaland delivered a monologue of over two minutes detailing the teams he represented in the years covered by the Premier League's investigation into Man City, as the star questioned how he was meant to respond to the club's guilty verdict.
    • In a recent development, man City were found guilty of the vast majority of charges brought against them by the Premier League for financial wrongdoing when the verdict was released in September.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

    Published: 09:50 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 06:26 EST, 16 November 2026.

    Erling Haaland delivered a monologue of over two minutes detailing the teams he represented in the years covered by the Premier League's investigation into Man City, as the star questioned how he was meant to respond to the club's guilty verdict.

    In a recent development, man City were found guilty of the vast majority of charges brought against them by the Premier League for financial wrongdoing when the verdict was released in September. The club have since appealed.

    An independent commission ruled Man City had disguised payments worth £900million in a nine-year period with ‘sham’ deals.

    Man City were found to have artificially inflated sponsorship agreements and pumped money into the club from its Abu Dhabi owners via disguised payments in a bid to swerve Premier League spending rules.

    Haaland was quizzed about the club's situation by Norwegian broadcaster TV2, after scoring in the national team's 3-1 victory over Wales on Saturday.

    The Man City star's initial answer lasted for two minutes and 14 seconds, as he reeled off the teams he had represented from 2009 to 2018, the years covered by the charges.

    Erling Haaland insisted it was difficult for him to answer a question about Man City's guilty verdict, with the club appealing against the decision of an independent commission. Source: TV2Sport.

    Haaland stressed he remains happy at the club after being asked about his future given the potential ramificiations if Man City fail with their appeal to overturn the verdict.

    In a recent development, 'In 2009, I played for Bryne U9s. In 2010, the U10s. In 2011, the U11s. 2012, the U12s, 2013, the U13s. Shall we continue? We don't need the whole list. 2014, the U14s. 2015, the U15s and the national team,' Haaland began.

    Industry observers note that 'Then the U16s, I think. In 2016, I moved up to Bryne's first team, second team and youth team. In 2017, I went to Molde. In 2018, I was with Molde. The first team, Molde 2 and a bit with the youth team.

    'So this is a question I struggle to answer because it's a legal battle….

    'It's a case between the Premier League and Manchester City that a panel will deal with. Am I supposed to answer that? I'm not really sure.'.

    Haaland continued by listing fellow Norwegians who had been at Man City at the time, joking that they may be in a better place to offer insight.

    'There were quite a few Norwegians at the club during that period, I think,' Haaland noted.

    Recent findings suggest that 'Abdisalam Ibrahim, Martin Samuelsen and Omar Elabdellaoui were there. Kjetil Haug was there too. I think there were a couple more but I can't remember.

    The forward distanced himself from the case as he listed team he played from 2009-18, the time covered by the charges. Pictured: Haaland in action for Molde in 2018.

    'But it's a difficult question to answer when I don't really know that much about it.

    'I assume the answers will come… I don't know when. I haven't read much about it.

    'To be completely honest, I'm focused on trying to perform for Manchester City.

    It has been revealed that 'A club I signed a five-year deal with in 2022 and a latest nine-and-a-half-year deal in late 2024. I think that claims everything about the matter. I'm a City player, and I'm incredibly happy there.'.

    Man City have continued to insist they had 'irrefutable evidence' proving their innocence, but if the club loses its appeal, the Premier League have a range of sanctions at their disposal – including relegation or expulsion.

    Haaland, who has won eight major honours at the club including the Treble in 2023, was asked about whether the case has affected his thoughts on his Man City future.

    'I understand that you want a little headline here, but as I stated, I signed a long-term contract in 2024,' Haaland responded.

    'I'd say I made a pretty good choice by joining City in 2022. We can all agree on that. I won't say it myself, but look at the trophies I've won and how I've developed on and off the pitch.

    'I'm standing here after winning an international 3-1 and we're top of our group in Europe.

    In a recent development, 'Things aren't going so well for City in the league, but we'll try to turn that around against Fulham. But we can't focus on that now. Now we have to focus on Denmark.'.

    Man City have won twice and lost three times in the Premier League since the independent commission verdict was announced in September.

    Enzo Maresca's side have slipped to six points behind reigning champions Arsenal following their drop off in form.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • As we emerge from the recent General Manager Meetings and move toward the expected Dec.
    • Industry observers note that the decorated lefty, who soon turns 30, is our No.
    • Industry observers note that "Excluding Yoshinobu Yamamoto, who was a special case as a Japanese star with no MLB track record, Skubal is the best starting pitcher to hit free agency since Gerrit Cole in 2019.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    As we emerge from the recent General Manager Meetings and move toward the expected Dec. 1 lockout of the players by MLB owners, we might see an accelerated pace of activity soon. The most tantalizing possibility is that ace and two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, the undisputed top talent on the free agent market this winter, will sign before the sport shuts down for an indeterminate amount of time.

    Industry observers note that the decorated lefty, who soon turns 30, is our No. 1 free agent of the 2026-27 class, and it's not an especially close call. Here's part of our write-up:.

    Industry observers note that "Excluding Yoshinobu Yamamoto, who was a special case as a Japanese star with no MLB track record, Skubal is the best starting pitcher to hit free agency since Gerrit Cole in 2019. He showed few long-lasting effects from the NanoScope elbow surgery in May and remains a capital-A Ace with terrific surface stats and under-the-hood performance indicators. Skubal brings four swing-and-miss pitches to the table (four-seamer, changeup, slider, curveball), a near MLB-best ability to limit exit velocity, and elite strike-throwing ability (MLB's third-lowest walk rate since 2023). Build an ace starter in a lab and he would look a lot like Skubal. He'll play the entire 2027 season at age 30, and given the things teams can do with pitchers these days, Skubal figures to remain a frontline starter for most of a long-term contract. He's the only true balance-of-power player available in free agency this offseason. Skubal can swing a division race and a postseason series all by himself.".

    It has been revealed that will he set the record for the biggest contract ever signed by a pitcher? Will Skubal fetch the highest average annual salary for a pitcher? Will he top $400 million? Those are all reasonable questions to ask. First, though, there's a question to be asked about the teams that are already pursuing him the most vigorously. That question is, which team needs him the most? We're restricting our discussion to the five teams that have been most reliably linked to Skubal so far this offseason. We're already hearing reports of surprise teams, and it's always possible a surprise late bidder will enter the fray and even win his signature, but for now, these five clubs are the favorites. This, then, is an ordering of those teams based on which desperately needs a talent like Skubal in order to reach their goals in 2027 and beyond. Let's get to it, in order from "needs him the most" to "needs him but not as urgently as the teams ahead of them" ….

    The Cubs are in contention mode and in need of roster improvements if they're going to run down the world champion Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Central. The rotation is without question the most pressing need for Chicago. Shota Imanaga, Matthew Boyd, David Peterson, and deadline acquisition Clay Holmes are all free agents. Justin Steele hasn't taken the mound at the significant-league level since early in the 2025 season thanks to UCL surgery and a halting recovery process. While he's expected to be ready for 2027, he's not exactly a known quantity right now. Young upsider Cade Horton may not be back until midseason after undergoing Tommy John surgery, and Ben Brown, who recently had neck surgery, may be on a similar timeline. So, yes, the Cubs need a lot of rotation help, and Skubal would give them the true frontline ace they'd lack even if everyone were healthy. Unfortunately for the Cubs fans, it sounds like the Ricketts aren't willing to be truly competitive for his services.

    According to recent reports, coming off the grave disappointments of 2026, the Mets could certainly use a headline-grabbing addition to improve their chances in 2027 and inspire a surely disaffected fan base. Beyond that, the Mets need more starting pitching to accompany promising young Nolan McLean. Christian Scott seems like a lock, but he doesn't project as a frontliner. They have some depth options for the back end, but they need a true needle-mover like Skubal at the very front. That's especially the case in what figures to be a hotly competitive NL East in 2027. Thus far, David Stearns and owner Steve Cohen sound committed to making a good-faith run at Skubal.

    The Padres have a lot of work to do if they're going to earn a fourth straight playoff appearance. Speaking of which, the rotation is crying out for help right about now. They lost Dylan Cease to free agency last winter, and this time Michael King may be bound elsewhere, too. The Pads declined their club option on Nick Pivetta, and while they hope to bring him back on more favorable terms, there's no guarantee they'll be able to do that. Yes, Joe Musgrove will be back, but how much can he give them and how effective will he be? They'll need even more help if Adrian Morejon, a lockdown bulk reliever and possible starter-conversion project, signs elsewhere. Skubal's made to order, and signing the top talent on the market would be a strong signal by new owners José E. Feliciano and Kwanza Jones that the team's recent tradition of spending and contending won't be fading away.

    The Dodgers self-evidently needed Skubal enough to acquire him from the Detroit Tigers leading up to the deadline and do so at significant cost. On paper, the Dodgers aren't as desperate for rotation help as the teams ahead of them on this list, but there's still a need. Yoshinobu Yamamoto is a certifiable ace, but behind him Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow are established health and durability risks. Shohei Ohtani is something of an unknown, at least insofar as his pitching is concerned right now, and thus far Roki Sasaki and Emmet Sheehan have not proved worthy of being relied upon. One can squint and see the Dodgers' current championship window closing in the reasonably near future, which means that's all the more reason to push the chips in now. Retaining the elite services of Skubal would greatly aid the cause in 2027.

    According to recent reports, eyeball a rotation that already includes Dylan Cease, José Soriano, and Trey Yesavage, and you might think it doesn't need much more. And maybe it doesn't. As a matter of principle, though, any team with contending aspirations should be interested in a top-shelf ace when he hits the market. The Jays, who in recent years have invested in the roster at commendable levels, are no doubt dreaming of a Skubal-Cease one-two punch that would be the envy of, oh, every other team in baseball. There's also depth to think about. In particular, Cody Ponce is a bit of an unknown coming off knee surgery that ended his 2026 season in the middle of his first start. Addressing the offense probably should be more of a priority for the Jays this winter, but, again, it's Tarik Skubal, and the likes of Tarik Skubal make any team better.
